Apple has reportedly cut orders for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max due to "sluggish demand." A recent report from Nikkei Asia says Apple has informed select suppliers to reduce component production for these two models, with the price hikes allegedly "dampening consumer demand."

Price hikes reportedly curbing iPhone 18 Pro demand

The report cites "multiple informed sources" and says Apple has "taken a more conservative stance on shipments since early September." Two of those sources say component orders in October were cut by "at least 15%" from Apple's original requirements.

Another anonymous supply chain manager told Nikkei Asia that demand is "not as strong as when all new models used to launch simultaneously." This, of course, refers to the fact that Apple won't unveil the base iPhone 18 until spring next year. Suppliers note, however, that this factor alone does not fully account for the weak demand.

Top comment posted by Hallmark

Every time we hear these "reports" about production cuts, when the financials come out, it's a record quarter.

Every time this year there are reports of weak demand, Apple on the other hand continues to grow its revenue.

I won't be quick to believe these "reports" unless the actual numbers reflect it.

One of the sources added that the "iPhone Duo" is expected to face "a similar fate" after launch, meaning it may also see production cuts.

Apple raised the price of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max by US$100 over the previous generation. Although the move has dampened demand, the report also notes that the slowdown "may not immediately translate into a decline in Apple revenue."

Apple will report its fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 results on Monday, November 6, which will offer an early look at demand for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max in their first weeks on sale.
